title: Concentrating Viruses by Tangential Flow Filtration
author: Steven W Wilhelm
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbagiibw

steps.title: Set up TFF apparatus with filter
steps.instruction: Attach the Pellicon XL 30 kDa filter (catalog number PXC030C50) to the tangential flow filtration (TFF) apparatus and connect both the retentate and waste tubes so they empty into a waste flask.

steps.title: Prepare 0.1 N NaOH solution
steps.instruction: Make 500 mL of 0.1 N NaOH at 45 °C and pour the solution into the TFF reservoir.

steps.title: Start pump and set pressures
steps.instruction: Turn the pump speed to 1 or 2, then rotate the back‑pressure valve clockwise until the bottom pressure gauge reads 30‑40 psi and the top gauge reads approximately 10 psi.

steps.title: Circulate NaOH until 350 mL remains
steps.instruction: Run the NaOH through the system, circulating fluids until about 350 mL remains in the reservoir; re‑attach the retentate tube to circulate the remaining cleaning solution that does not pass through the filter; continue running NaOH for ~20 minutes, ensuring the system never runs dry.

steps.title: Stop pump at 50 mL and empty NaOH
steps.instruction: When only ~50 mL of NaOH is left, turn the pump off, tighten a plastic clamp onto the tubing leading to the pump inlet, detach the tube, undo the clamp, and empty the remaining NaOH into a waste vial (see Figure 2).

steps.title: Remove residual NaOH with syringe
steps.instruction: Attach a syringe to the tube connecting the pump outlet, pull back the plunger to draw out any residual NaOH inside the machine; re‑attach the tubing and repeat with the syringe to drain any other tubing (e.g., over the filter surface).

steps.title: Wash system with MilliQ water
steps.instruction: Flush the TFF system with at least 1 L of MilliQ water: let the first 500 mL exit through both retentate and waste tubes, then re‑attach the retentate tube to circulate the remaining 500 mL for ~10 minutes; finally empty the remaining volume using the same syringe‑drain procedure as in steps 5 and 6.

steps.title: Prime system with Tris‑MgCl₂ buffer
steps.instruction: Circulate 300 mL of 50 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 7.8) containing 10 mM MgCl₂ until about 25 mL remains; this primes the TFF system to protect viruses from residual NaOH.

steps.title: Concentrate virus stock and recover
steps.instruction: Fill the reservoir with the virus stock and run the system at the same pressures (bottom 30‑40 psi, top ~10 psi). After concentration, empty the remaining reservoir volume into a Falcon tube. If virus adheres to the filter, attach a syringe to the pump‑out tube and draw out the remaining fluid, moving the plunger back and forth as needed to dislodge virus.

steps.title: Purify concentrated virus sample
steps.instruction: Purify the concentrated virus as appropriate (e.g., filter‑sterilize for axenic cultures or perform a sucrose density gradient for non‑axenic samples).

steps.title: Determine virus titer by plaque assay
steps.instruction: Titer the sample by plaque assay and compare the measured concentration to the theoretical value, where theoretical concentration = (V₁ × C₁) = (V₂ × C₂).

steps.title: Clean TFF system post‑run
steps.instruction: Clean the TFF system with NaOH following the same procedure used in the preparation steps, then rinse thoroughly with MilliQ water.

steps.title: Store filter with cold NaOH
steps.instruction: Using a syringe filter, fill the Pellicon filter with 0.1 N NaOH and keep it at 4 °C until the next use.
